output.summary: KEP-2590 proposed a new --subresource flag for kubectl get, patch, edit, apply and replace so users can fetch and update status, scale and resize subresources without kubectl --raw or curl. Per the status, it is implemented and at stage stable; apply support was dropped from the alpha scope.
output.rationale: Fetching and patching subresources previously required kubectl --raw or curl, which the readme calls cumbersome and not user-friendly. The flag makes status, scale and resize first-class in kubectl while keeping the API contract identical to the full resource. During alpha review, SIG-CLI limited scope to get, patch, edit and replace because apply with a subresource is tricky, since last-applied annotations are not captured for subresources.

alternatives.option: Use curl or kubectl --raw to update subresources directly
alternatives.why_not: The readme calls this method cumbersome and not user-friendly, and says patching subresources with kubectl was not possible at all.

alternatives.option: Include apply in the alpha scope
alternatives.why_not: soltysh suggested limiting alpha to get, patch, edit, replace given the tricky nature of apply, and ykakarap agreed to limit the scope to those commands.

alternatives.option: Add an alpha- prefix to the flag name
alternatives.why_not: soltysh did not like this approach because the flag name would have to change eventually; nikhita chose a description that explicitly calls out alpha instead.

evidence.quote: This document proposes adding a new `--subresource` flag to the following kubectl subcommands: `get`, `patch`, `edit`, `apply` and `replace`.
Given the tricky nature of `apply` I will limit the scope to only `get, patch, edit, replace` for the alpha stage.
It's totally fine, just add a note, that due to additional complexity and the nature of `kubectl apply` command we've decided not to expand it with this flag.
This enhancement is now marked as `Tracked for code freeze` for the {current release} Code Freeze!
